@babyblueviper1 Good complement — between the three (AnchorRegistry, OpenTimestamps, RFC 3161), Phase 1 now has a real menu of layer-3 trust models instead of one default: a rollup's own consensus (no named party, cheap, no batching), Bitcoin PoW (trust-minimized, delayed until the proof is upgraded, no submitter recorded), and a named TSA (immediate, precise, trust concentrated in the TSA's key).

Your composition point is the one worth keeping for the schema: a record carrying more than one existence bound should report each separately, and a disagreement between them is a signal, not noise
